# Ball-Possession Inference from Automatic Tracking — Team Westside

**Competition:** More than a Hack 2027, Phase 1 — FC Barcelona vs Athletic Club
**Submission file:** `Westside.csv` (regenerated byte for byte by the repository; see section 8)

## 1. Overview

The task is to label every frame of the match as home possession (H), away possession (A) or
dead ball (D). Because the ranking metric scores possession *spells* — continuous intervals of one
label — rather than individual frames, we model possession as a sequence of intervals.

Our system is a deterministic pipeline built around the provided tracking data. Each component
produces a per-frame score for the three states, and a semi-Markov decoder converts these scores
into intervals with realistic durations. Decoding runs in two passes: the first decides whether
the ball is in play, and the second decides which team has it while it is in play.

We chose this design over an end-to-end learned model for three reasons: there is a single test
match with no labels, the ball is missing on 41% of graded frames, and the tracking has its own
characteristic errors. Every component therefore had to be interpretable, testable on other
matches, and robust to missing data. All parameters and models were selected on external matches
(Metrica Sports sample games and the DFL Bundesliga open dataset) and on automatic consistency
checks; no human labels on the provided match were used at any stage.

## 2. Method

### 2.1 Input preparation

| Step | Description | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ball trajectory repair | Removes implausible jumps and outliers, interpolates short gaps and predicts briefly across very short occlusions. | `possession/trajectory.py` |
| Broadcast alignment | Aligns the broadcast tracking to the tactical timeline by matching player formations; time offsets are estimated at run time and replays are detected and excluded. | `possession/broadcast.py` |
| Broadcast ball fill-in | Where the tactical ball is missing but the aligned live broadcast tracking sees it, the broadcast position is used if a player is within 1.5 m and the implied speed is at most 15 m/s. | `possession/broadcast.py` |
| Team assignment of tracks | Corrects two kinds of tracking identity errors: goalkeeper tracks that follow the opposing keeper, and outfield tracks whose kit colour in the video contradicts their metadata team. | `possession/tracking.py`, `tools/audit_track_teams.py` |

### 2.2 Signals used to infer possession

| Signal | Description | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Player proximity | Distance from the ball to the nearest players of each team and local team density around the ball. | `possession/tracking.py` |
| Ball touches | A player within 1.5 m of the ball at a sharp change in its direction is treated as a touch; that team keeps possession until the next touch, for at most 2 s, or until the ball is about to disappear from tracking. | `possession/decoder.py` |
| Dead-ball detection | The ball leaving the pitch (until it is seen back in play), kickoff formations, set pieces reported by Smart Tagging, broadcast cutaways of at least 5 s, and stoppage patterns in player movement. | `possession/decoder.py`, `possession/tagging.py`, `possession/broadcast.py` |
| Smart Tagging | Tagged phases indicate a team; defensive phases (*Defending in … third*, *Defensive transition*) indicate the opponent of the tagged team. | `possession/tagging.py` |
| Ball-free model | A small one-dimensional CNN reads about ±3 s of player tracking and an approximate ball position, and predicts which team has the ball. It is used while the ball is missing and when no player is within 1 m of it. Inference uses NumPy only. | `possession/ballfree_seq.py`, `models/ballfree_seq_ball_cnn3.npz` |
| Video: team at the ball | During tactical ball gaps, a ball detector and a person detector run on the tactical video; the kit colour of the player at the ball identifies the team. Used for the team decision only. | `tools/extract_team_at_ball.py` → `evidence/team_at_ball_gaps.npz` |

### 2.3 Temporal model

A semi-Markov model with minimum interval durations combines these signals. Changing team costs
10 units, reduced to 2.5 when the change is supported by an observed touch or hand-over. In the
first pass the model decides in play versus dead; in the second pass the dead intervals are fixed
and only the team is chosen, so the ball-free model and video signals can influence which team
has the ball but never whether the ball is in play.

## 3. Possession rules

- **Ball in or out of play.** The ball is dead only when there is direct support for it: it left
  the pitch and has not been seen back, players are in kickoff formation, a set piece is tagged,
  the broadcast cuts away from play, or players show a stoppage pattern. Each half is dead from
  the start of its graded period until the automatically detected kickoff.
- **Change of possession.** Possession belongs to the team that last touched the ball. Loose
  balls, deflections and 50/50 contests do not change possession on their own; a change requires
  a touch, an observed hand-over or sustained evidence from the ball-free model or the video.
- **Duels.** Duels cannot be resolved reliably from tracking (simple attribution rules were right
  only 53–58% of the time on external matches), so without a following touch the previous team
  keeps possession.
- **Restarts.** Throw-ins, corners, goal kicks and kickoffs end a dead-ball period, and the team
  tagged for the restart is favoured immediately afterwards.
- **Ball not tracked.** The team is inferred from the players' configuration and, where
  available, from the video.
- **Goalkeepers.** A metadata goalkeeper track within 30 m of the opponent's goal is assigned to
  the team defending that goal, because the two goalkeeper tracks swap identities in this data.

## 4. Data sources

| Source | Used | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tactical tracking (ATD) | Yes | Main input: ball, players and teams. |
| Tactical homography | Yes | Projects tracked positions into the video for the video signals. |
| Smart Tagging | Yes | Restarts, restart team and phase-based team indication. |
| Broadcast tracking and homography | Yes | Alignment, cutaway detection and ball fill-in. |
| Tactical video | Yes, offline | Detection and kit colour via `tools/`; the outputs are committed in `evidence/`, so the submission can be regenerated without the video. |
| Broadcast video | No | Tested for ball detection, team at the ball, scene types and replays; no improvement. |
| Public 5-minute ground truth | Format checks only | Never used for tuning or model selection. |

**Approaches tested and not adopted** (measurements in `docs/benchmarks/`): ball positions
detected in the tactical or broadcast video; replay and scene-type detection; restart timing from
video; video team-at-ball on frames where the ball is tracked; hidden semi-Markov and state-machine
decoders; per-half decoding; duration priors; minimum spell durations and removal of short spells;
model ensembles; carrying possession through ball flight; control-phase segmentation; filtering
tags by type; letting the ball-free model trigger team changes on tracked frames; shifting or
bridging interval boundaries; giving the ball-free model corrected track teams; and a corrected
touch-detection window with additional cues for ball reappearance.

## 5. Training data

| Dataset | Source and licence | Labels produced by | Size | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Metrica Sports sample games 1–3 | metrica-sports/sample-data (public) | Provider event data; we derive possession intervals from passes, carries, recoveries and stoppages | 3 matches | Training the ball-free model, fitting coefficients, validation |
| DFL Bundesliga open dataset (Bassek et al.) | Official release, CC BY 4.0 | Provider ball-status and possession flags | 4 matches for training and development (J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY); 3 for diagnostics (J03WPY, J03WQQ, J03WR9) | Training the ball-free model, simulation of challenge conditions |
| Kit-colour classifier | Provided match | Automatic: detected people are matched to tracked players by position; no human decisions | 3,000 sampled frames | Team of a detected person in `tools/` |
| Missing-data patterns | Provided match (counts and masks only; no positions or labels) | — | Graded frames | Making the external training data look like the challenge tracking |

Our team produced no labels that are used anywhere. Two touch events in SoccerTrack v2 were
checked by hand during early exploration; they are not used by any model, parameter or the
submission.

## 6. Validation

The challenge score cannot be measured before submission, so each change had to improve results
on checks that are independent of the test labels. The primary metric throughout is the challenge
metric: mean one-to-one possession-spell F1 over IoU thresholds 0.3–0.7.

1. **External matches** (`validation/fast_eval.py`). For each Metrica sample game, 60 fixed
   regression checks (spell F1 at several IoU thresholds, boundary recall, frame accuracy) under
   eight degradation scenarios, plus spell F1 on the DFL matches. The *Metrica validation score*
   quoted below is the composite of these checks, not the challenge metric itself.
2. **Simulated challenge conditions** (`validation/proxy_eval.py`). DFL matches, whose true
   possession is known, are degraded to resemble the challenge tracking by replaying the
   challenge's own pattern of missing players and missing ball, optionally with ball-position
   noise. A further noise model was fitted to touch statistics measured on the challenge tracking
   without labels. Learned models are always evaluated on matches they were not trained on.
3. **Consistency checks on the provided match** (no labels involved):
   - *Masking test:* the tracked ball is hidden in windows where it was visible, the pipeline is
     re-run, and the output is compared with its own output on the full data.
   - *Touch reliability:* how often the team of a detected touch also controls the ball next.
   - *Robustness suite:* 134 automatic checks of determinism, stability under small input
     perturbations and plausible structure.
4. **Decision procedure.** Each candidate change, and the criteria it had to meet, was fixed
   before it was scored. Every adopted change keeps the previous configuration and output as a
   fallback.

**Changes adopted, with their measured effect** (details in `docs/benchmarks/` and in the
`working_submission_selection` section of each `configs/submission_*.json`):

| Change | Measured effect |
| --- | --- |
| Touch-based possession carry | DFL spell F1 +0.06 to +0.11 on all seven matches |
| Ball-free model during ball gaps, then the sequence CNN | Spell F1 with the ball hidden improved on all 10 external matches |
| Lower cost for supported team changes | Metrica validation score +0.014 to +0.033 |
| Corrected interpretation of defensive Smart Tagging phases | Agreement between the tag signal and a decode without tags 0.63 → 0.73 |
| Touch radius 1.5 m | Simulated challenge conditions +0.019, 7 of 7 matches |
| Goalkeeper identity correction | Removes about 800 frames credited to the wrong team |
| Video signals (team at the ball, kit-colour track correction) | Masking test +0.005 to +0.040 |
| Ball-aware model | Metrica validation score +0.023 to +0.033; simulated challenge +0.022 to +0.032 (4 of 4 development matches); close to zero on clean data |
| Dead ball before each half's kickoff | Removes four false possessions before the second-half kickoff |

## 7. Limitations and future work

- **Unknown test score.** Our external references derive possession from provider events or
  flags, which may follow different conventions from the challenge ground truth. For example,
  delaying team changes by five frames improves DFL scores but lowers Metrica scores.
- **Broadcast cutaways** turn a substantial number of frames into dead ball. This rule could not be
  validated against true possession, because neither feed shows play during a cutaway.
- **Short possessions** such as interceptions and quick turnovers are the largest remaining source
  of error; on Metrica they account for most of the gap to a perfect team assignment.
- **Duels and aerial balls** cannot be resolved from tracking, so the previous team is kept.
- **Simulation fidelity.** The simulated challenge conditions match some properties of the
  challenge tracking but not all, and the three diagnostic DFL matches were evaluated many times,
  so they are not an unbiased test.
- **Touch detection** measures the incoming ball velocity one frame before the window it checks
  for visibility. Correcting this removed false touches when the ball reappears, but lowered
  Metrica spell F1 by about 0.01, so the submission keeps the original detector.
- **Video outputs** are bit-identical across NVIDIA L40S GPUs; CPU inference differs slightly, so
  the committed files in `evidence/` are the reference.

With more time we would model the restart taker explicitly, learn team changes at turnovers from
external event data, and validate the broadcast-cutaway rule on another match with both feeds.

## 8. Reproducing the submission

```bash
python3.9 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-pinned.txt
export MTAH_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/the/licensed/bundle
python -m possession.cli --output reproduction.csv      # about 20 s on CPU; no video or GPU
python evaluation/validate_submission.py reproduction.csv
cmp reproduction.csv Westside.csv                       # no output: byte-identical
```

Regenerating the video outputs (GPU) and the models, and the licences of third-party assets, are
described in [REPRODUCIBILITY.md](REPRODUCIBILITY.md). No language model is used by the pipeline;
an AI coding assistant was used during development.
